iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order starting Friday, October 16, but scammers are attempting to lure people to fake websites to place their orders early.

The malware-laden website is crafted to closely mimic the official page, and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an 'exclusive offer from an authorized partner'...

Security researchers at Malwarebytes pointed out that the webpage exploits the DarkSword vulnerability chain to compromise some older iPhones that have not installed the patch. Users do not need to perform any action; merely visiting the site is enough to trigger the attack.

Once the attack succeeds, hackers will harvest the user's device identification data and status, and attempt to transmit the list of installed applications along with the contents of Apple Notes. After completing this, the attack will shift its focus to cryptocurrency wallets.

It will subsequently attempt to access messages, contacts, call history, voicemail messages, emails, calendar entries, and cached location data. The malware can also contact its server to receive further instructions.

The exploit chain was publicly disclosed by Google as early as March this year, and Apple subsequently released a patch within the same month.

9to5Mac Take

The usual precautionary advice still applies: unless you trust the sender and expect to receive the relevant link, do not click on any links sent to you. Also be sure to install iOS updates immediately after they are released.
